verses.text: So all Israel was listed in family records, and these are written in the book of the kings of Israel. The people of Judah were taken away as prisoners to Babylon because they were unfaithful to God.
The first people to move back to their own land and towns were ordinary Israelites, priests, Levites, and temple servants.
Some people from the tribes of Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim, and Manasseh settled in Jerusalem.
From Judah there was Uthai son of Ammihud, the son of Omri, the son of Imri, the son of Bani. He was a descendant of Perez son of Judah.
From the Shilonites there was Asaiah, the firstborn, and his sons.
From the descendants of Zerah there was Jeuel. In all, there were six hundred and ninety people from Judah.
From the tribe of Benjamin there was Sallu son of Meshullam, the son of Hodaviah, the son of Hassenuah.
There was also Ibneiah son of Jeroham, Elah son of Uzzi, the son of Michri, and Meshullam son of Shephatiah, the son of Reuel, the son of Ibnijah.
Their relatives, as listed in the family records, numbered nine hundred and fifty-six. All these men were heads of their families.
From the priests there were Jedaiah, Jehoiarib, and Jachin.
There was also Azariah son of Hilkiah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Zadok, the son of Meraioth, the son of Ahitub. Azariah was the official in charge of God's temple.
There was Adaiah son of Jeroham, the son of Pashhur, the son of Malchijah. And there was Maasai son of Adiel, the son of Jahzerah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Meshillemith, the son of Immer.
There were one thousand seven hundred and sixty priests in all, heads of their families. They were very able men, responsible for the work of serving in God's temple.
From the Levites there was Shemaiah son of Hasshub, the son of Azrikam, the son of Hashabiah, a descendant of Merari.
There were also Bakbakkar, Heresh, Galal, and Mattaniah son of Mica, the son of Zichri, the son of Asaph.
There was Obadiah son of Shemaiah, the son of Galal, the son of Jeduthun. And there was Berechiah son of Asa, the son of Elkanah, who lived in the villages of the Netophathites.
The gatekeepers were Shallum, Akkub, Talmon, Ahiman, and their relatives. Shallum was their chief.
Until then they had been stationed at the King's Gate on the east side. They were the gatekeepers for the camp of the Levites.

Shallum son of Kore, the son of Ebiasaph, the son of Korah, and his relatives from his family, the Korahites, were in charge of guarding the entrances to the tent. Their ancestors had been in charge of guarding the entrance to the LORD's camp.
In earlier times Phinehas son of Eleazar had been in charge of the gatekeepers, and the LORD was with him.
Zechariah son of Meshelemiah was the gatekeeper at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.

In all, two hundred and twelve men were chosen to be gatekeepers at the entrances. They were listed in the family records in their villages. David and Samuel the seer had given them their positions of trust.
So they and their descendants were responsible for guarding the gates of the LORD's house, the house that was a tent.
The gatekeepers were on all four sides: east, west, north, and south.
Their relatives in their villages had to come from time to time and share their work for seven days at a time.
But the four chief gatekeepers, who were Levites, were given the job of trust. They were in charge of the rooms and the treasuries in God's temple.
They spent the night around God's temple, because they had to guard it. And they had to open it every morning.
Some of them were in charge of the objects used in the temple service. They counted them when they were brought in and when they were taken out.
Others were put in charge of the furniture and all the other holy objects, and of the fine flour, the wine, the olive oil, the incense, and the spices.
But some of the priests were the ones who mixed the spices.
A Levite named Mattithiah, the firstborn son of Shallum the Korahite, was trusted with baking the bread used for offerings.
Some of their relatives from the Kohathite clan were in charge of preparing the holy bread for the table every Sabbath.
Some were musicians, heads of Levite families. They lived in the temple rooms and did not have other duties, because they were busy with their work day and night.
All these were heads of Levite families, as listed in their family records. They were leaders, and they lived in Jerusalem.
Jeiel, the father of Gibeon, lived in Gibeon. His wife was named Maacah.
His firstborn son was Abdon. His other sons were Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, Nadab,
Gedor, Ahio, Zechariah, and Mikloth.
Mikloth was the father of Shimeam. They also lived near their relatives in Jerusalem.
Ner was the father of Kish. Kish was the father of Saul. Saul was the father of Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Eshbaal.
Jonathan's son was Merib-Baal. Merib-Baal was the father of Micah.
Micah's sons were Pithon, Melech, Tahrea, and Ahaz.
Ahaz was the father of Jarah. Jarah was the father of Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri. Zimri was the father of Moza.
Moza was the father of Binea. Binea's son was Rephaiah, Rephaiah's son was Eleasah, and Eleasah's son was Azel.
Azel had six sons. Their names were Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan. These were Azel's sons.
